_note: Tracked cross-unit threads. Per-thread shape (matches Matthew's data/threads.json): id, root, translit, gloss, example? (one quoted in-text usage, plain voice, no citations -- style reference §1, only when it clarifies the translation choice), color, status ('open'/'closed'), tagged (bool), opens {unit, ref}, payoffs [{unit, ref, note?}], note (prose). Each thread's `root` must also resolve to an entry in data/roots.json (a hand-curated set of Strong's/lemma ids, see pipeline/roots.py) before pipeline/audit_thread_coverage.py can audit it. candidates/retro are NOT thread.json fields -- those live per-unit in a fragment's unit-meta block (threads.candidates/threads.retro), see pipeline/unit_meta.py's module docstring. Promotion policy (2026-09-16, Lane): Claude decides book-wide vs. local per unit, biased toward book-wide (a thread kept local when payoff shows up later is worse than one tracked that never pays off); Claude asks Lane only when genuinely unsure. `payoffs` stays empty until the unit containing the payoff is actually built -- don't cite a ref in an unbuilt unit.

opens.note: natan ×8 in unit 1's speeches; Yahweh 'is giving' (participle) vs. 'Moses gave' (perfect) — the land as gift, already done and not yet done.

payoffs.note: The first voice after Yahweh's to say the land is already given is a Canaanite prostitute's — the gift confirmed from the far side of the wall.
The spies' whole report is Rahab's sentence handed back to Joshua: Yahweh has given the land into our hand.

threads.note: natan ×8 in unit 1's speeches; Yahweh 'is giving' (participle) vs. 'Moses gave' (perfect) — the land as gift, already done and not yet done.
threads.echo: Gen 12:7 — 'to your seed I will give this land,' the first promise to Abraham; Gen 15:18 draws its border to the Euphrates.

threads.gloss: cross over; the far side (of the Jordan)

opens.note: the book's first command, qum ʿavor 'rise, cross' (1:2), relayed down the chain (1:11); ʿever 'far side' marks the eastern tribes as people of the other bank. One root, both ids.

payoffs.note: ʿever, 'the far side of the Jordan' — spoken from Jericho's bank, Sihon and Og are the ones across the river.
Two men cross the Jordan ahead of the nation — a small, secret crossing before the great public one of unit 3.

threads.note: the book's first command, qum ʿavor 'rise, cross' (1:2), relayed down the chain (1:11); ʿever 'far side' marks the eastern tribes as people of the other bank. One root, both ids.
threads.echo: Deut 3:25–27 — Moses begs, 'let me cross over and see the good land,' and is told 'you will not cross this Jordan.' Deut 31:3 — 'Joshua will cross before you.'

opens.note: Qal yarash 'possess' only in unit 1; the Hiphil 'drive out' arrives later in the book — the stem split is the thread.

threads.note: Qal yarash 'possess' only in unit 1; the Hiphil 'drive out' arrives later in the book — the stem split is the thread.
threads.echo: Gen 15:7 — 'to give you this land to possess it,' to Abraham; Deut 1:8 — 'go in and possess the land.'

threads.gloss: cause to inherit, give as an inheritance

opens.note: tanḥil 'you will cause to inherit' (1:6) is the first naḥal-family word in the book, ahead of naḥalah 'inheritance' in the allotment chapters (units 13-20).

threads.note: tanḥil 'you will cause to inherit' (1:6) is the first naḥal-family word in the book, ahead of naḥalah 'inheritance' in the allotment chapters (units 13-20).
threads.echo: Deut 1:38; 3:28; 31:7 — three times Moses says it: Joshua is the one who 'will make Israel inherit' the land.

opens.note: meniaḥ 'giving rest' (1:13) and yaniaḥ (1:15) set up the book's completion formula (21:44, 22:4, 23:1).

threads.note: meniaḥ 'giving rest' (1:13) and yaniaḥ (1:15) set up the book's completion formula (21:44, 22:4, 23:1).
threads.echo: Gen 8:4, 9 — the ark comes to rest (nuaḥ), and the dove finds no resting place; Deut 12:9–10 — rest promised as the goal of the land. Heb 4:8 — 'if Joshua had given them rest, God would not speak of another day.'

opens.note: ḥazaq ×4 — three times from Yahweh, the last time from the eastern tribes (1:18); recurs at 10:25.

threads.note: ḥazaq ×4 — three times from Yahweh, the last time from the eastern tribes (1:18); recurs at 10:25.
threads.echo: Deut 31:6–7, 23 — 'be strong and be firm' is Moses' charge to Israel and to Joshua, then Yahweh's, before Joshua 1 repeats it.

threads.gloss: be firm, be resolute (the glottal ʾ, aleph — not the ʿ of ʿavar)

opens.note: ʾamats, always paired with ḥazaq; kept as its own root per the colour policy (split pairs).

threads.note: ʾamats, always paired with ḥazaq; kept as its own root per the colour policy (split pairs).
threads.echo: Deut 3:28 — Yahweh to Moses: 'charge Joshua, make him strong and make him firm.'

threads.gloss: instruction, the Torah (here 'the scroll of the torah')

opens.note: 'the scroll of the torah' (1:8) opens a line to 8:31-34, 22:5, and 23:6.

threads.note: 'the scroll of the torah' (1:8) opens a line to 8:31-34, 22:5, and 23:6.
threads.echo: Deut 31:24–26 — Moses writes the torah in a scroll and has it laid beside the ark. 2 Kgs 22:8 — 'I have found the scroll of the torah,' in Josiah's temple.

opens.note: ʿeved YHWH belongs to Moses in unit 1; watch whether and when Joshua receives it (24:29).

threads.note: ʿeved YHWH belongs to Moses in unit 1; watch whether and when Joshua receives it (24:29).
threads.echo: Deut 34:5 — 'Moses the slave of Yahweh died there'; Josh 24:29 finally gives Joshua the same title, at his own death.

opens.note: 'wherever you send us we will go' (1:16) — the next verse in the book, 2:1, is Joshua sending the spies.

payoffs.note: 'Wherever you send us we will go' (1:16) — the very next act in the book is Joshua sending, quietly, two men; by 2:3 the king of Jericho is sending too.

threads.note: 'wherever you send us we will go' (1:16) — the next verse in the book, 2:1, is Joshua sending the spies.
threads.echo: Num 13:2–3, 17 — Moses sent twelve men to spy out Canaan, Joshua among them. Joshua's first act as leader repeats it with two.

opens.note: first ḥaram in the book, in Rahab's mouth, before Israel has devoted a single Canaanite city; becomes the governing law of Jericho, Ai, and the campaign reports.

threads.note: first ḥaram in the book, in Rahab's mouth (2:10), before Israel has devoted a single Canaanite city; becomes the governing law of Jericho, Ai, and the campaign reports.
threads.echo: Deut 7:2; 20:17 — 'you shall devote them to destruction,' the law; Deut 2:34; 3:6 — its first practice, on Sihon and Og.

opens.note: Yahweh's oath to the fathers (retro'd — untagged when unit 1 was built).

threads.note: Oaths bind the book together: Yahweh's oath to the fathers (1:6), Rahab's oath (2:12, 17, 20), its keeping (6:22), the Gibeonite oath (9:15, 19-20), the rest formula (21:43-44).
threads.echo: Gen 26:3 — 'the oath which I swore to Abraham'; Deut 1:8 — 'the land Yahweh swore to your fathers.'

opens.note: 'his blood on his head' — the bloodguilt logic the cities-of-refuge law runs on.

threads.note: 'his blood on his head' (2:19) is the bloodguilt logic the cities-of-refuge law runs on — the blood-avenger of 20:3, 20:5, 20:9.
threads.echo: Lev 20:9 — 'his blood is on him,' the formula for bloodguilt; Num 35:33 — blood pollutes the land. Matt 27:25 — 'his blood on us and on our children.'

opens.note: 'our heart melted' — fear, returning for the Amorite/Canaanite kings and, reversed, for Israel after Ai.

threads.note: Melting hearts: Rahab's 'our heart melted' (2:11) returns for the Amorite and Canaanite kings (5:1) and, reversed, for Israel after Ai (7:5).
threads.echo: Deut 1:28 — forty years earlier, the first spies' report 'made our heart melt.' Now it is Canaan's heart. Deut 20:8 — the faint-hearted go home before battle, 'lest his brothers' heart melt.'

opens.note: 'Chase after them, fast' — Rahab sends Jericho's men chasing the wrong way; the book's first chase is a decoy.

threads.echo: Exod 14:8–9 — Pharaoh chased after the sons of Israel to the sea; Josh 24:6 remembers it. Deut 32:30 — 'how could one chase a thousand?', turned into promise at Josh 23:10.
threads.note: Chasing: Jericho's decoy chase (2:5–22) turns into Israel's own routs (7:5, where Israel is the one chased; 8:16–24; 10:10, 19; 11:8), the blood-avenger who chases the manslayer to a city of refuge (20:5), 'one of you chases a thousand' (23:10), and Egypt chasing the fathers to the Reed Sea (24:6).
